author: xiaokuerz
title: fix(audio): reset stale fade state when GainNode is reused/reconnected

questions.prompt: ResetFadeState sets fadeInState_ = true but collFadeInState_ = false. Why the asymmetry -- why is a fade-in triggered for the main fade path but not for the collaboration fade path?

options.text: fadeOutState_==DONE_FADEOUT is a per-frame silence gate in SignalProcess, so a reused node was muted; fade-in avoids the silence->full-volume pop. collFadeOutState_==DONE_FADEOUT is NOT a silence gate (DoCollFading only acts on DO_FADEOUT), so no fade-in is needed; coll fade-in is driven by SetCollFadeState, not by reconnect.
Both should be true for symmetry; collFadeInState_ = false is a bug that will be fixed in a follow-up.
fadeInState_ = true ensures audio starts muted and ramps up gradually; collFadeInState_ = false because collaboration mode is always disabled during reconnect.
fadeInState_ must be true because SignalProcess refuses to process audio when it is false; collFadeInState_ being false is harmless since no collaboration session is active.

questions.explanation: The code comment explains: DONE_FADEOUT in fadeOutState_ causes SignalProcess to silence every frame, so the reused node was permanently muted. Setting fadeInState_=true ramps from low volume to full, avoiding the pop. In contrast, collFadeOutState_==DONE_FADEOUT is not a silence gate -- DoCollFading only acts on DO_FADEOUT -- so clearing to NO_FADEOUT is sufficient; coll fade-in is driven by collaboration logic (SetCollFadeState), not reconnect.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- the asymmetry is intentional: main fade-out is a silence gate requiring fade-in; coll fade-out is not.

questions.prompt: Before this change, the old code was `if (!SafeGetMap(idGainMap_, sessionId)) { ... create ... }` with no else branch. What would happen when CreateGainNode was called for a sessionId that already had a GainNode?

options.text: The existing node was replaced with a fresh HpaeGainNode, losing all state but avoiding the stale-fade bug.
The existing node was silently reused with its stale fade state -- if it had DONE_FADEOUT from a previous Pause, SignalProcess would continue silencing every frame on the reused node.
The function was a no-op since the if-guard was false, and SignalProcess would automatically detect and clear DONE_FADEOUT on the next frame.
The old code would create a duplicate entry in idGainMap_, causing a memory leak and undefined behavior.

questions.explanation: The old code had no else branch -- when SafeGetMap found an existing node, the if-body was skipped and the function returned, leaving the existing node untouched. This means stale fade state (e.g. DONE_FADEOUT left by a Pause) persisted into the node's next lifecycle, and SignalProcess would keep silencing every frame because DONE_FADEOUT is a per-frame silence gate. The fix adds an else branch that calls ResetFadeState() to clear the stale state.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- the missing else branch was the root cause: stale DONE_FADEOUT survived into the node's next lifecycle.

questions.code: operation_ = OPERATION_INVALID; // clear stale op; harmless (SetFadeState reassigns before use)
questions.prompt: The comment says setting operation_ to OPERATION_INVALID is "harmless (SetFadeState reassigns before use)". If operation_ were NOT cleared here and left stale (e.g. a previous fade-out operation), what would be the actual risk?

options.text: The stale operation could trigger an immediate fade-out on the next SignalProcess call, causing audio dropouts until SetFadeState is called.
SignalProcess reads operation_ directly to decide whether to silence data, so a stale operation value would mute audio on every frame.
In practice, no harm -- SetFadeState always reassigns operation_ before it is read, so the stale value would be overwritten before use; clearing is purely defensive.
It would cause a null pointer dereference because OPERATION_INVALID maps to an uninitialized pointer internally.

questions.explanation: The comment explicitly states that SetFadeState reassigns operation_ before it is used. This means the codebase guarantees operation_ is always set via SetFadeState before SignalProcess reads it. If ResetFadeState did not clear operation_, the stale value would simply be overwritten by the next SetFadeState call. Clearing to OPERATION_INVALID is defensive -- it makes the intent explicit and avoids confusion if someone reads operation_ between ResetFadeState and the next SetFadeState.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- clearing operation_ is defensive, not a correctness requirement; SetFadeState overwrites it before use.

questions.code:
sessionGainNode->ResetVolume();
    sessionGainNode->ResetFadeState(); // clear stale fade (e.g. DONE_FADEOUT) on reconnect
questions.prompt: A reconnect path may call both CreateGainNode (which calls ResetFadeState on the reused node) and then ConnectInputCluster (which also calls ResetFadeState). What is the effect of the second ResetFadeState call?

options.text: The second call overwrites the fade-in ramp that the first call started, causing an audio pop on reconnect.
Harmless -- ResetFadeState is idempotent; it sets every field to the same default value, so calling it twice produces the same state as calling it once.
The second call accumulates fadeProcessedBytes_ (0 + 0 = 0 is fine, but a third call would add again), producing an incorrect fade curve.
It causes a data race because both calls modify the same shared_ptr without synchronization.

questions.explanation: ResetFadeState unconditionally assigns each field to a fixed default (fadeOutState_=NO_FADEOUT, fadeInState_=true, fadeProcessedBytes_=0, etc.). It does not read-then-increment; it overwrites. So calling it N times produces the same state as calling it once. The fade-in ramp is not 'started' by ResetFadeState -- it is driven by SignalProcess reading fadeInState_==true, which happens after both reset calls are done.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- ResetFadeState is idempotent: all fields are unconditionally overwritten, not accumulated.

questions.prompt: The comment says "DisConnect erases the node, so reuse is unlikely, but reset for parity/defense." If DisConnect always erases the node, why was the ResetFadeState call added here at all?

options.text: For parity and defense -- even though DisConnect normally erases the node, there may be edge cases (error paths, unexpected call sequences) where the node survives, so resetting is a safety net that also keeps the two CreateGainNode implementations consistent.
Because DisConnect only erases the node on certain device types; on virtual device types the node persists and must be reset.
Because the code must mirror HpaeProcessCluster exactly to maintain binary compatibility across the two cluster types.
Because DisConnect is deprecated and will be removed in a future release, which would leave stale nodes that need resetting.

questions.explanation: The comment explicitly says 'parity/defense': parity means matching HpaeProcessCluster's behavior (which also resets on reuse), and defense means guarding against unexpected cases where the node is not erased by DisConnect (e.g. error paths, reordering of calls). The code is a safety net, not a fix for a known recurring scenario.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- 'parity/defense' means consistency with the other cluster + guard against edge cases where DisConnect does not fire.

questions.prompt: After ResetFadeState, the test asserts EXPECT_NE(..., 0.0f) -- the last sample is not zero. Why doesn't the test assert EXPECT_EQ(..., UT_UNIT_GAIN) instead, given FillBuffer filled the input with UT_UNIT_GAIN?

options.text: Because floating-point arithmetic in SignalProcess introduces precision errors, so the output can never be exactly UT_UNIT_GAIN.
Because SignalProcess applies its own volume scaling (curGain_) that is independent of the input gain, so the output is not expected to match UT_UNIT_GAIN.

Because ResetFadeState sets fadeInState_=true, SignalProcess applies a fade-in ramp -- the output starts below UT_UNIT_GAIN and ramps up, so the last sample may not equal UT_UNIT_GAIN; the test only verifies data is not silenced (not zero).
Because the fade-in ramp starts at full volume and decays to zero, so the last sample could be any value between 0 and UT_UNIT_GAIN.

questions.explanation: ResetFadeState sets fadeInState_=true to trigger a fade-in on reconnect (avoiding the silence->full-volume pop). When SignalProcess processes the next frame, it applies the fade-in ramp, meaning the output starts below the target gain and ramps up over totalFadeBytes_. So the last sample of the first frame after reset is not at UT_UNIT_GAIN -- it is somewhere in the ramp. EXPECT_NE 0.0f is the correct assertion: it verifies the data is not silenced (the bug) without over-constraining to the exact ramp value.
questions.reinforce: Correct -- fadeInState_=true means SignalProcess ramps up, so the output is not at full gain yet; the test only checks it is not silenced.
